READ-ONLY confirmed: nothing in /home/user/skill-do-work was edited, staged or committed. The scanner was copied to the scratchpad to run it, and the checkout is untouched.

WHY THE DEFECT IS REAL HERE, NOT THEORETICAL
_dev/tests/prescribed-shell-harness.sh:9 sets `set -uo pipefail`, and every one of the 19 case files sources it. So pipefail is on for all 90 sites. (Note it is `-uo`, not `-euo`: there is no `-e`, which is why a nonzero assertion line does not abort the run - it just produces the wrong verdict.)

Family B is exactly the shape REQ-593 measured. Its self-check at _dev/tests/update-script-behavior.sh:121-135 builds a 256 KiB shell variable and drives the shipped matchers over it; the fixed form is `grep -Eq -- "$pattern_text" <<<"$probe_output"` (line 97). So the printf-builtin-replaying-a-variable producer is the proven case, and the herestring is the sanctioned conversion for it.

DIRECTION OF THE WRONG ANSWER, PER ASSERTION POLARITY
Of the 90 sites, 62 are positive (`|| fail_case`) and 28 are negative (`&& fail_case`). The two directions fail differently and the negative one is worse:
  - Positive: grep matches (0), producer dies of SIGPIPE (141), pipefail returns 141, `||` fires -> spurious FAIL. Noisy, so someone eventually looks at it.
  - Negative: grep matches (0) meaning the defect IS present, producer dies (141), pipefail returns 141, `&&` does not fire -> the defect passes SILENTLY. This is the one that lets a real regression through.
The negative sites that guard something worth guarding: protected-inventory.sh:19 (a quarantined secret path must never appear in association output), all 21 find sites (private scratch/staging must not leak), qualify.sh:368 (the fixture index must be clean), qualify.sh:183 (a gitignored file must not be scanned), audit 103/170/195/215/242/262 and repair 195/344 (refused stamps must not be logged as corrections).

WHY NO CONVERSION HERE NARROWS AN ASSERTION - WITH ONE EXCEPTION
The REQ-593 review hazard is a herestring throwing away a producer's exit status. It does not apply to Family B, because the producer in the pipeline is `printf` replaying an already-captured variable, and printf of a variable carries no information. The real producer ran earlier inside `$( )`, and in 66 of the 68 Family B sites its status is already asserted on the capture line with `|| fail_case '... returned nonzero'` or `&& fail_case '... passed when it should not'`. The two captures with no status assertion are qualify.sh:217 and qualify.sh:297, and that is deliberate - those cases measure the warning text, not the exit code - so the conversion changes nothing there either.

The exception is qualify.sh:368, the only site in the slice whose pipeline producer is a real external command: `git -C "$qualify_repo" diff --cached --name-only | grep -q 'cell_renderer' && fail_case`. A naive `grep -q 'cell_renderer' <<<"$(git ...)"` discards git's status, and this is a negative assertion, so a git failure would become an unconditional pass on the check that the fixture index stayed clean - precisely the truncated-tar narrowing REQ-593's review caught. Convert it in two steps, asserting git's status explicitly (see that entry's safe_conversion). That form is strictly better than what is there now, because the current pipeline already swallows a git failure the same way.

FAMILY A IS THE SHAPE BUT NOT THE HAZARD
All 21 `find ... -print -quit | grep -q .` sites carry `-quit`, so find prints at most one path (60-120 bytes) and exits before grep can outrun it. There is no measurable SIGPIPE window at any tree size, because -quit bounds the OUTPUT, not the traversal. They still deserve conversion - the scanner flags them, and reviewers should not have to re-derive the -quit argument each time - but they are cleanup, not a live bug. `[ -n "$(find ... -print -quit)" ]` is the direct replacement and preserves what each one measures ("did find print anything").

One small extra at publish-portfolio-summary.sh:40: the find target directory is expected not to exist, so find writes to stderr and exits 1 on the passing path. Add `2>/dev/null` while converting. Do not promote find's nonzero status to a failure there - a missing snapshots directory is the pass.

TWO SITES NEED MORE THAN A HERESTRING
audit-archive-timestamps.sh:170 and 195 are three-stage: `printf | grep -E '(would repair|repaired) ' | grep -q REQ-nnn`. Replacing only the first stage still leaves `grep -E | grep -q`, where the middle grep is itself an early-leaving reader's writer. Capture the filtered lines into a variable first, then herestring the second grep. Do not collapse the two greps into one `grep -qE 'A.*B'` - that adds a left-to-right ordering constraint the two-grep form does not have, which would quietly weaken a refusal-parity check.

MECHANICAL NOTES FOR WHOEVER APPLIES THIS
- Patterns using `$'...'` ANSI-C quoting (protected-inventory.sh:16, :18, lexical-memory-recall.sh:12) work unchanged off a herestring.
- `printf '%s'` emits no trailing newline; `<<<` appends one. For every pattern in this slice that is a no-op, because grep treats a final incomplete line as a line and none of these patterns is anchored to end-of-input.
- Keep the grep dialect as-is per site. repair-req-timestamps.sh:195 uses BRE alternation `'REQ-811\|REQ-812\|REQ-813'`; audit 170 uses `-qE`. Converting the pipe form is not an invitation to change the dialect.
